title: Erdős #866 and the trivial uniform lower bound
content: Erdős #866 asks for the minimal threshold g_k(N) such that every A ⊆ {1,…,2N} with |A| ≥ N + g_k(N) contains all pairwise sums b_i + b_j of some k-element family. The known landscape is non-uniform: g_3 = 2, g_4 ≤ 2032, g_5 ≍ log N, g_6 ≍ √N, with gaps and most cases open. The simplest universal obstruction is parity: the N odd numbers in {1,…,2N} form a half-density set whose pairwise sums are systematically excluded (sum of equal-parity numbers is even). The docstring states up front that this file proves only the trivial lower bound g_k ≥ 1, generalizing the base file's single k=3 lemma to all k ≥ 3, and makes no claim on the deep, open content of #866.
mathContext: $g_k(N)$: least $g$ with $|A| \ge N+g \Rightarrow A$ contains all pairwise sums of some $k$-family. Parity gives $g_k(N) \ge 1$ uniformly.

title: The odd numbers are a subset of the interval
content: oddNumbers_subset records that oddNumbers N ⊆ Erdos866.Interval N, immediate from Finset.filter_subset since oddNumbers N is defined in the base file by filtering the interval {1,…,2N} on the odd-parity predicate. This is the small but necessary containment that lets the odd numbers serve as a witness set inside the interval in every downstream lemma — exists_large_set_without_config and not_guarantees_zero both consume it.
prerequisites: oddNumbers as a filter of the interval (base file)

title: oddNumbers_no_config: the uniform parity obstruction
content: For every k ≥ 3, ¬∃ b : Fin k → ℤ, HasAllPairwiseSums (oddNumbers N) b. This generalizes the base file's oddNumbers_no_triple (k=3) to all k ≥ 3. Proof: assume a family b. First, every pairwise sum landing in the odd numbers is an odd natural ((b i + b j).toNat % 2 = 1), read off from oddNumbers membership. Then restrict to the indices 0,1,2 : Fin k, which exist because k ≥ 3 (built as ⟨0,_⟩,⟨1,_⟩,⟨2,_⟩ with ordering via Fin.mk_lt_mk). The three sums b0+b1, b0+b2, b1+b2 must all be odd; but among b 0, b 1, b 2 two share parity, so one sum is even — and omega, which understands Int.toNat and mod 2, derives the contradiction in a single call. The key reduction is that a k-configuration constrains the pairwise sums of its first three members, so every k ≥ 3 collapses to the triangle case.
mathContext: Among $b_0, b_1, b_2$ two share parity $\Rightarrow$ one of $b_0{+}b_1, b_0{+}b_2, b_1{+}b_2$ is even $\Rightarrow$ not odd $\Rightarrow$ contradiction.

title: Packaging the witness and the threshold predicate
content: exists_large_set_without_config bundles the odd numbers as a witness set of size ≥ N (via oddNumbers_card) inside the interval with no k-configuration, so |A| = N never forces one. Guarantees N k g is then a Prop capturing the threshold semantics — every A ⊆ {1,…,2N} with |A| ≥ N+g forces some k-configuration. Defining the bound through this predicate rather than as an infimum keeps the statements first-order and omega-friendly while still faithfully expressing 'g_k(N) ≥ 1': any g that genuinely guarantees a configuration must beat the size-N odd witness.
mathContext: $\mathrm{Guarantees}(N,k,g) :\equiv \forall A \subseteq \{1,\dots,2N\},\ |A| \ge N{+}g \Rightarrow \exists\,k\text{-family with all pairwise sums in } A$.

title: The lower bound g_k(N) ≥ 1
content: not_guarantees_zero refutes g = 0: the odd witness has size N = N+0 and no configuration, so a threshold of 0 cannot guarantee one. g_k_ge_one then concludes that any g with Guarantees N k g satisfies 1 ≤ g — by the dichotomy g = 0 ∨ g > 0, the g = 0 branch is killed by not_guarantees_zero. This is the formal statement of the elementary lower bound g_k(N) ≥ 1, now uniform over all k ≥ 3 where the base file had only the k = 3 parity lemma. The headline #866 conjecture (exact growth of g_k for k ≥ 4) remains open and is untouched.
